vulnerabilities.description: Missing per-user authorization checks. All handlers use `assertCharacterBatchOperationAllowed()` which appears to be a feature flag, not per-user resource authorization. No validation that the requesting user owns/can access the batchId, characterId, or promptPackId being operated on. This allows any authenticated user to access any resource.

Insufficient input validation on resource IDs. While code checks `typeof req.query?.batchId === 'string'`, it doesn't validate ID format, length, or structure. Could enable NoSQL injection or enumeration attacks if using document DBs or similar stores.

Missing validation of array item structure. Code iterates `body.jobs` with minimal validation per item. No validation of `job.promptId`, `job.promptPackId`, or `job.characterId` format before processing.

No validation of numeric parameters. `targetCount`, `maxNewCandidates` passed without type/range validation. Could be negative, extremely large, or non-numeric, causing backend errors or resource exhaustion.

Potential information disclosure in error responses. Error messages include operation names (`'CHARACTER_BATCH_GET_ERROR'`) and rely on `normalizeHandlerError()` which may expose stack traces or implementation details.
No visible request size limits or rate limiting. Large POST payloads could cause denial of service. No throttling on batch generation or ComfyUI queue operations.
Unsafe nested optional chaining. `raw?.queue?.queue_running.some()` doesn't validate the intermediate objects exist before calling `.some()`. Should validate structure before method calls.
Conditional trim() without null check. `body.workflowId.trim()` could throw if `body.workflowId` is null/undefined despite the typeof check (type coercion edge case).
Missing CSRF protection. No visible CSRF token validation on POST requests. If frontend is CORS-enabled to external origins, vulnerable to cross-site attacks.
No audit logging. Operations like approve, reject, save candidates have no logged trail of who performed the action and when.

recommendations: **CRITICAL**: Implement per-user authorization. Add user context (userId/claims) to all requests. Validate that the user owns or has explicit permission for each resource (batchId, characterId, promptPackId) before processing.
Implement strict input validation schema (Zod, Joi, or similar) for all request parameters. Validate ID format (UUID, alphanumeric range), numeric ranges, enum values.
Add request size limits (e.g., `express.json({ limit: '1mb' })`) to prevent DoS via large payloads.
Implement rate limiting on sensitive operations (batch generation, ComfyUI queue, ingest) using tokens or sliding windows.
Sanitize error responses - return generic error messages to clients, log detailed errors server-side only. Never expose operation names or implementation details.
Add CSRF protection: require CSRF tokens on all state-changing operations (POST/PUT/DELETE), validate origin headers.
Implement audit logging: log userId, operation, resource IDs, timestamps for all batch operations.
Add Content-Type validation - explicitly check `req.headers['content-type']` includes 'application/json' before parsing.
Validate all nested object structures before method calls - replace `?.some()` with explicit existence checks.
Fix optional chaining edge case in `comfy-validate-workflow.js` line 14 - validate `body.workflowId` exists before calling `.trim()`.
Document and review the `normalizeHandlerError()` function - ensure it doesn't leak stack traces or sensitive context.
Add database connection security: validate that `createVectorRuntime()` properly closes connections even on error (already using finally blocks, good).
